subject: Helios Health: request for extended forensic log retention & evidence handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@helioshealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: security@helioshealth.com
Date: 2027-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: extended log retention (forensics) + evidence for SIG/SOC2

Hi Stephanie,

Quick one from our InfoSec team — we run periodic forensic reviews tied to incident response and regulatory audits. Our standard retention requirements are 180 days for ingestion logs and application trace logs. I see Redwood's default log TTL is 30 days in the hosted offering; can you confirm if Helios can get an exception to preserve logs for 180 days for the tenant "helios-prod"?

Specifically we need:
- Confirmation of exact log types retained (request logs, task traces, audit events)
- A mechanism to pull a verified export (hashed) or a log-escrow snapshot at intervals
- Evidence artifacts we can attach to our SIG/SOC2 submission (signed statement, sample extracts, retention policy wording)

Attaching a short PDF that our auditor provided with the evidence checklist. Can you let us know what you can supply and whether this requires a DPA/DLP amendment or a managed exception? Also include timeline — we need the artifacts consolidated by May 5 if possible.

Thanks,
Jordan Park
Sr. Security Program Manager
Helios Health

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@helioshealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended log retention (forensics) + evidence for SIG/SOC2

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the checklist. Looping in Marcus (Security Ops) and Laura (Compliance) to size this and confirm deliverables.

High-level: Redwood supports customer-specific retention profiles for Dedicated and Private deployments today; for hosted tenants we can assemble a managed exception and provide periodic escrowed snapshots + signed attestations. We need to confirm scope (exact log streams) and whether Helios expects continuous 180d retention in-place vs. a periodic escrow/archive.

Marcus / Laura — please review the attached checklist and Jordan's timeline. Can we commit to an initial evidence package by May 5 and a formal exception amendment within two weeks? Also clarifying question for Jordan: do you need searchable access to logs for 180 days, or is a hashed escrow + ability to deliver extracts sufficient for your auditor?

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-23T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended log retention (forensics) + evidence for SIG/SOC2

Stephanie / Laura — reviewed Jordan's checklist. Proposed plan and artifacts: 

1) Scope: we will include request logs (http access logs), inference trace metadata (model, seq len, request id), and control-plane audit events for tenant helios-prod. Exclude payloads containing PII unless Helios confirms a specific consent/TOU amendment.

2) Retention approach: for hosted: create a managed exception where logs are exported to a secure, read-only S3 bucket under Redwood's escrow project. We will retain that bucket for 180 days and provide a hashed manifest of daily snapshots. This avoids changing live TTLs and keeps production performance stable.

3) Evidence artifacts to deliver (initial package by 2027-05-05):
   - Signed statement describing retention exception and scope (redwood_log_exception_signed.pdf)
   - Daily snapshot manifest with SHA256 hashes (sample_manifest.csv)
   - One hashed sample export covering a 7-day window (helios_sample_export_7d.tar.gz)
   - Technical runbook describing export/export verification (redwood_log_escrow_procedure.pdf)
   - Access logs for the escrow bucket showing integrity checks

4) Legal/compliance: Laura — will this require a DPA amendment or a simple exception addendum? We should also prepare a DocuSign exception form for Helios to sign (I can draft).

5) Security controls: export buckets will be encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys where available; we will include key metadata in the manifest.

Open questions for Helios: searchable access vs. escrow-only (Jordan please confirm). Also confirm whether Helios needs chain-of-custody notes for any future incident use.

Attachments: evidence_artifact_inventory.csv, redwood_log_escrow_procedure.pdf

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@helioshealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: security@helioshealth.com
Date: 2027-04-27T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended log retention (forensics) + evidence for SIG/SOC2

Stephanie / Marcus — this all looks good and addresses the auditor checklist. Quick clarifications:

- Escrow snapshot approach is acceptable; we do not need live searchable retention as long as we get verified daily snapshots and a clear chain of custody.
- We do require a signed exception addendum (DocuSign) referencing tenant helios-prod and the 180-day window. Please include the KMS key id used for encryption in the manifest.
- Timeline: evidence package by May 5 is great. Once we have the DocuSign envelope and the initial package we can mark this as complete for SIG purposes.

Please send the DocuSign link to me and cc our legal (security@helioshealth.com). Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Jordan
Sr. Security Program Manager
Helios Health
